test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 15 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What is the name of the portal launched by the Reserve Bank of India in May 2025 for the regulated entities (REs) to report details of their digital lending apps (DLAs)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Centralised Information Management System (CIMS)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** launched a dedicated portal on its **Centralised Information Management System (CIMS)** in **May 2025** to maintain a repository of **Digital Lending Apps (DLAs)**.
 
• This initiative requires all **Regulated Entities (REs)**, such as **Banks** and **Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs)**, to report and regularly update information regarding the **DLAs** they use or outsource for lending activities.
 
• The primary objective of this portal is to provide a **verified list** of authorized apps to the public, thereby protecting consumers from **unauthorized** or **illegal lending apps** that often engage in predatory practices.
 
• The **CIMS** repository includes critical data points such as the **name of the app**, the **name of the RE** it is associated with, the **web link** of the app, and the **official logo**.
 
• By mandating this reporting, the **RBI** aims to enhance **transparency** and **accountability** within the rapidly growing **Fintech** ecosystem in **India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Centralised Information Management System (CIMS):**
 
 
• **CIMS** is the **RBI's** next-generation **data warehouse**, which was initially launched to replace the older **XBRL (eXtensible Business Reporting Language)** based reporting system.
 
• It utilizes advanced **Big Data** analytics and **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** to manage the vast amounts of financial data generated by the **Indian banking sector**.
 
• The system serves as a **single source of truth** for regulatory reporting, **monetary policy** analysis, and **financial stability** monitoring.
 
 
 
• **Digital Lending Landscape in India:**
 
 
• **Digital Lending** refers to the process of offering loans through web platforms or mobile apps, often using **automated technologies** for credit assessment.
 
• The **RBI** issued comprehensive **Digital Lending Guidelines** in **September 2022** to regulate the flow of credit and ensure **Consumer Protection**.
 
• In **2024-2025**, the surge in **unauthorized apps** led the government and **RBI** to tighten the **Whitelisting** process for apps allowed on the **Google Play Store** and **Apple App Store**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regulatory Compliance:** Any **DLA** that is not listed on the **CIMS** repository by its respective **Regulated Entity** can be flagged as **unauthorized** by law enforcement agencies.
 
• **Data Security:** **REs** are responsible for ensuring that their **DLAs** comply with **data localization** norms and the **Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023**.
 
• **Consumer Redressal:** The portal complements the **RBI's Ombudsman Scheme** and the **Sachet Portal**, which is used for reporting **illegal financial activities**.
 
• **Transparency:** The public can access the repository to verify if a lending app is genuinely partnered with a **licensed bank** or **NBFC** before sharing personal documents.
